ch40.d.N: Total number of atoms sent out of the oven one by one
ch40.s.d.model: Classical prediction (magnetic moment in any direction) or the actual result (quantized spin)
ch40.s.goal.quant: After a non-uniform magnetic field the beam splits into just two parts: the spin component $S_z$ can only be $\pm\hbar/2$
ch40.s.goal.classical: Classically the magnetic moment can point any way, so a continuous band is expected on the screen
ch40.s.obs.band: Classical prediction: a band spread evenly up and down
ch40.s.obs.two: Actual: two lines, up ($\uparrow$) and down ($\downarrow$), nothing in between
ch40.s.obs.random: Which way a single atom goes cannot be predicted; many atoms split half and half
ch40.s.assume.atom: Spin-½ atoms (like silver, one outer electron); spins leave the oven in random directions
ch40.s.assume.view: Schematic: deflection and beam width are not to scale. The + exit is drawn up and the − exit down whatever the device axis
ch40.q.d.setup: Measuring axes of the Stern-Gerlach devices in sequence
ch40.q.d.pass: Exit of the second (x) device sent on to the next device; the other exit is blocked
ch40.q.goal.repeat: Measuring again along the same axis gives the same result
ch40.q.goal.erase: Measuring along another axis (x) erases the information from the earlier z measurement
ch40.q.obs.zz: z → z: pass only +z at the first device and the second z device gives + every time
ch40.q.obs.zx: z → x: a +z state measured along x gives +x and −x half and half
ch40.q.obs.zxz: z → x → z: although −z was blocked, half the atoms come out −z at the last device
ch40.q.obs.pass: Passing −x instead of +x still gives half and half at the end
ch40.q.assume.ideal: Ideal devices: no atoms lost, only two exits; atoms at a blocked exit stop (the number beside it counts them)
ch40.a.d.theta: Angle $\theta$ between the second device's axis and the $z$ axis (in the zx plane)
ch40.a.goal.prob: Measuring a +z state along the direction $\theta$ gives + with probability $\cos^2(\theta/2)$
ch40.a.goal.random: Each atom's result is random and only the fraction can be predicted; more atoms bring it closer to the prediction
ch40.a.obs.N: Graph: the running fraction swings widely at first, then settles on the dashed prediction; the error bar shrinks as $1/\sqrt{N}$
ch40.a.assume.plane: The measuring axis turns only within the zx plane
